sources.fact: The Week (Oct 28, 2015): the Tea and Consent video was released by Thames Valley Police as part of the #ConsentIsEverything campaign; don't make someone drink tea they don't want; don't pour tea down an unconscious person's throat; 'Consent: it's as simple as tea'
IBTimes UK (Oct 28, 2015): Thames Valley Police animation published on YouTube on 27 October 2015 as part of the #Consentiseverything campaign

Devon Sexual Health (NHS): if someone is asleep, unconscious or under the influence of drugs or alcohol they can't consent; you can change your mind at any time, consent can be withdrawn at any time during sexual activity and each time activity occurs; sex in the past does not mean consent in the future

Rape Crisis England & Wales: people who are asleep, unconscious, drunk or on drugs lack capacity to consent; we all have the right to change our minds at any time; being married or in a relationship makes no difference, you still need consent every single time; if someone stays quiet or doesn't respond they are not agreeing
Queensland Health: people who are asleep, drunk, high or passed out cannot consent; you can change your mind at any stage; if a party is silent, there is no consent

math.note: Thames Valley Police Tea and Consent video, published 27 Oct 2015 (IBTimes UK, The Week)

post.instagram_caption:
British police once explained consent with a cup of tea ☕

In 2015, Thames Valley Police released a video comparing consent to offering someone tea. If they say no thanks, don't make them tea. Someone who is asleep, drunk or passed out can't consent. People can change their mind at any time, a yes last time doesn't mean yes now, and silence isn't a yes.

If you can understand tea, you can understand consent.

Sources: Thames Valley Police via The Week, NHS Devon Sexual Health, Rape Crisis England & Wales, Queensland Health.
